title: Storyboard relay
review: One repair, with remaining flaws
note: Muse establishes the postal robot. Nano Banana stages the next scene but duplicates its seedling. Gemini identifies that error; Muse Edit receives both frames and the critique, removes the duplicate plant and improves the pose. A fresh Gemini review still flags the closed hatch. This is a fixed revision demonstration with visible limits, not a guarantee of perfect continuity.

inputs.label: First scene
inputs.text: First frame of an original two-scene story. A tiny postal robot has a rounded cream enamel body, one round amber eye, short dark-blue legs, and an orange mail satchel. It carries one clear glass capsule containing a single bright-green seedling. Outside a locked circular hatch of an abandoned orbital greenhouse, the robot reaches toward the small mechanical latch beside the door with one gripper while holding the capsule securely with the other. Dormant vines are visible through frosted glass; a curved station window reveals a black starfield. Wide 3:2 medium shot with the full robot, capsule and hatch visible. Tactile stop-motion miniature photography, indigo shadows and warm amber practical light. One robot and one capsule. No lettering, captions, split screen, panel borders or watermark.

inputs.label: Next beat
inputs.text: Create the next story beat inside the greenhouse. The robot is now crouched beside a circular soil tray, carefully placing the same bright-green seedling into the soil with one gripper; its other gripper holds the opened, now-empty glass capsule. The orange satchel remains visible. The round hatch stands open behind it. Frame the planting action clearly in a new medium shot. This is a visibly different action and location within the same world, not a restyle or wider crop of the doorway scene. Retain the tactile miniature look and indigo/amber light. No lettering or extra characters.

inputs.label: Continuity rules
inputs.text: Keep the same robot's rounded cream body, single round amber eye, dark-blue legs, orange satchel and relative proportions. Track the one glass capsule and one green seedling: the closed capsule in frame 1 should be opened and empty during planting in frame 2, with no duplicate seedling or capsule. Keep the miniature materials and indigo/amber lighting recognizable. Frame 1 shows an arrival at a closed hatch; frame 2 must clearly show planting inside after the hatch opens.

outputs.label: 2. Nano Banana: the draft duplicates the seedling

No robots, space stations, glass capsules, plants, text, panel borders or watermark.

title: Idea to concept art to 3D model
review: Orbited in the editor
note: GLM 5.3 Flash turns a one-line object idea into a concept description: a teal capsule-shaped toy submarine with a cream belly band, a brass periscope, three cream-rimmed portholes, a brass wind-up key, and a striped tail cone with a three-blade propeller. Join adds fixed render rules (one whole object, three-quarter view, plain light-gray background, no props), and Muse paints the concept. TRELLIS.2 (1024 geometry, 1024 textures, about 80k faces) turns that single picture into a 3.6 MB textured GLB. Orbiting it in nanoodle's 3D viewer shows a complete toy from every side, including a far side and back that the picture never showed: portholes on both flanks, the striped tail, the propeller blades, the key, and the periscope. Flaws: the viewer renders it flatter and less glossy than the concept, the thin key and propeller blades go soft at some angles, and the cream band on the far side is a plainer flat strip. Inspired by @patchmonkeydev's prompt → concept → multi-view → 3D ComfyUI pipeline on X; no media from that post is used.

title: Day to night between two keyframes
review: A real sunset timelapse that lands on the night keyframe
note: Muse paints a paper-craft seaside village at midday: six card houses, a striped lighthouse, two folded paper boats and a paper sun. Muse Edit repaints the same shot at night, with lit windows, the lighthouse lamp on, a paper crescent moon and stars. MiniMax H3 Max gets the day still on its image port and the night still on its end-frame port. Across 5 seconds the camera holds still while the sun sinks behind the trees, the sky goes from blue through orange and pink to navy, the windows light up and the lighthouse switches on. The clip ends on the night keyframe. It is the gallery's first start + end frame example. Flaws: the night keyframe turned the layered paper waves into glossy real-looking water, so the water changes material during the clip. The moon and stars appear only in the last second instead of fading in, and the lighthouse gives a soft glow, not a sweeping beam. The 480p setting was dropped by the headless runner (it sends resolution only when it has the model catalog), so the clip rendered at H3 Max's default 768p for $0.40. The saved graph says 768p to match. H3 Max also added a faint ambient sound bed. Swap either keyframe for a 📷 Image input to morph between your own before and after. Every keyframe and sampled video frame was checked and is SFW (paper scenery, no people). Inspired by @Audrius1454663's open-source rebuild of Higgsfield's VFX presets, Day→Night among them, on the Comfy Developer Platform (https://x.com/Audrius1454663/status/2111177673842012349). No media from that post is used.

title: A composer that watches your film
review: The fitted score enters on the first spark and is still playing when the lanterns rise; the blind one fades out early
note: MiniMax H3 Max Turbo films 10 silent seconds of a lantern on a still mountain lake at night: a firefly drifts down, the lantern lights, and a wave of lanterns lights and rises across the water. Frames pulls one still per second, and Elorian Glimpse reads them and writes a composer's brief with tempo, key, instruments and cue points ("at 4 s, when the lantern ignites, strings swell"). ElevenLabs Music composes from that brief and Soundtrack lays it on the film. A second branch scores the same film from a text description only, so you can hear what watching adds. All four of Glimpse's cue points land within about half a second of the picture, and the fitted cue tracks the asked 60 BPM. Flaws: ElevenLabs ignored the 10 s duration on the fitted call and returned 19 s, so the fitted version stops at 10 s while still at full level. The hush asked for at 3 s is only a small dip. Glimpse sees 1 fps stills, so it called the firefly a spark. The clips were re-encoded for the gallery. Every sampled frame was checked and is SFW (lanterns on a lake, no people).

title: Prompt to an editable SVG sticker
review: A baby dragon sticker as a real SVG, 122 vector shapes and no embedded raster
note: FLUX.3 Klein paints a sticker of a baby dragon holding a paper lantern in a flat style on a white background. Ideogram Vector, in convert mode with a blank prompt, turns that image into an SVG with 122 vector shapes and no embedded raster, so you can zoom to 8× and the edges stay crisp, then edit the shapes in any vector tool. Flaws: the prompt asked for four flat colours, but FLUX added soft shading and a white sticker border, and the vectorizer kept them faithfully, so the SVG has about 25 fills and 5 gradients rather than a minimal palette. The sticker PNG was re-encoded to WebP for the gallery; the SVG is as returned. Inspired by @AllaAisling's Ideogram Vector post (https://x.com/AllaAisling/status/2113305041906061472). No media from that post is used. Every image was checked and is SFW (a cartoon dragon).
